facts.label: Debt structure
facts.text: - Instruments are mostly secured. Secured debt is 25,575 of 29,321 in Note 5 and is made up of term loans under the 2013, 2014 and 2023 credit facilities, 7.25% and 5.75% senior secured notes, the AAdvantage Financing, EETCs, equipment loans and special facility revenue bonds (Q3 page:14 and page:15). Secured financings are collateralized by aircraft, engines, simulators, airport gate leasehold rights, route authorities, airport slots, certain receivables, certain intellectual property and certain loyalty program assets (Q3 page:16). - The only unsecured debt in Note 5 is the three PSP promissory notes, 3,746 in total. In the contractual obligations table they sit under AAG Parent and Other AAG Subsidiaries and fall due in 2030 and 2031 (Q3 page:66), so they are a parent-level claim that is outside the American maturity table. American's own table totals 25,575 of principal, equal to the secured subtotal. - Two loan families are tied to the AAdvantage loyalty program: the AAdvantage Financing is borrowed by American and AAdvantage Loyalty IP Ltd. and carries a peak debt service coverage ratio (Q3 page:17 and page:61). - Rates: the named term loans and PSP notes are floating (5.94% to 6.76% at September 30, 2026) and total 10,869, 37% of Note 5 debt before counting variable-rate equipment loans, which are inside the 4,926 line. - Bonds versus loans: the senior secured notes outstanding are the 7.25% notes (750) and the 5.75% notes (2,750); the 8.50% notes (1,000) were prepaid in full and the 5.50% notes (583 at year end) are nil at September 30, 2026. Most of the remaining debt is bank term loans, EETC pass-through certificates (9,332, up from 6,912) and equipment loans, not capital markets bonds. - 2026 financing activity (Q3 page:16 to page:20, page:45 and page:46): revolving commitments of the 2013, 2014 and 2023 facilities were reset to mature in March 2031; the 2014 term loans due January 2027 were refinanced to May 2033 with 703 of incremental term loans; the 2025 AAdvantage term loan margin was reduced; 8.50% secured notes of 1.0 billion and the 629 senior short-term term loan were repaid; 310 of EETC equipment notes were prepaid; and about 4.1 billion of EETC, equipment loan and other note proceeds were raised, including 2026-1, 2026-2 and engine EETCs. Of the 2026-2 EETC proceeds, about 633 remain in escrow and are not reported as American debt (Q3 page:19). - Maturity profile (American principal): 631 in the remainder of 2026, 3,550 in 2027, 7,861 in 2028, 3,884 in 2029, 972 in 2030 and 8,677 from 2031 (Q3 page:65). The 2028 column is the largest single year and is more than twice the 2027 figure. The sources do not break the 2028 amount down by instrument; named instruments due in 2028 in Note 5 are the 2013 term loan (960, February), the 7.25% notes (750, February) and the 2021 AAdvantage term loan (2,247, April), which do not explain the whole column because installment and equipment debt also amortizes into 2028. Remainder of 2026 through 2028 principal totals 12,042 against available liquidity of 11,797.

Of the 2026-2 EETC proceeds, about 633 remain in escrow and are not reported as American debt (Q3 page:19).

- Maturity profile (American principal): 631 in the remainder of 2026, 3,550 in 2027, 7,861 in 2028, 3,884 in 2029, 972 in 2030 and 8,677 from 2031 (Q3 page:65). The 2028 column is the largest single year and is more than twice the 2027 figure. The sources do not break the 2028 amount down by instrument; named instruments due in 2028 in Note 5 are the 2013 term loan (960, February), the 7.25% notes (750, February) and the 2021 AAdvantage term loan (2,247, April), which do not explain the whole column because installment and equipment debt also amortizes into 2028. Remainder of 2026 through 2028 principal totals 12,042 against available liquidity of 11,797.

facts.label: Liquidity and covenants
facts.text: - Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was 11,797 for AAG and 11,763 for American, comprising cash 1,124, short-term investments 7,163 and undrawn facilities 3,510 (Q3 page:59 and page:60). One 350 revolver was extended to March 2028 and a 50 cargo receivables facility expires in December 2026 (Q3 page:16), so undrawn capacity of 3,510 is not all long-dated. - Covenants are described, not quantified: loan to value or collateral coverage ratio covenants with cure through additional collateral, cash held in accounts, paydown or a higher interest rate; a minimum of 2.0 billion of unrestricted cash plus availability under revolving facilities in a significant portion of agreements; and a peak debt service coverage ratio in the AAdvantage Financing that can trigger early repayment. Management states compliance at the latest measurement dates (Q3 page:61). Thresholds, test dates and headroom are not in the supplied text. - The liquidity covenant row above uses cash plus undrawn facilities only and omits short-term investments, because the covenant text does not say whether they count; it shows ample indicative headroom but is not a covenant calculation. - The reported improvement in liquidity since year end coincides with a larger air traffic liability and loyalty program liability, which the 10-Q names as the main driver of nine-month operating cash flow (Q3 page:61). That inflow is seasonal and customer-funded; it is not earnings-driven.

facts.text: - Revenue rose 19.3% to 16,335 on yield and loyalty, with load factor down 2.6 points and capacity up 4.2% (Q3 page:43, page:44 and page:47). Fuel expense rose by 1,868 to 4,635 on a 62.7% higher price per gallon, absorbing the revenue gain; operating income fell to 115 from 151 and the pre-tax loss widened to 334 from 142. No fuel hedges were outstanding (Q3 page:44). - Non-fuel cost pressure: management's CASM excluding special items, fuel and profit sharing rose 3.0% to 14.34 cents; salaries, wages and benefits rose 252 and other operating expenses rose 237 (Q3 page:47 and page:50). - Net loss of 269 included pre-tax net special items of 112, mainly an impairment of the equity investment in Republic Airways Holdings and mark-to-market losses on equity investments (Q3 page:51). Interest expense, net was essentially flat at 435. - Derived discrete Q3 operating cash flow was negative and discrete Q3 capex was the largest of the year (CALC C7), after strong first-half inflows, which includes the first-quarter operating cash flow of 4,223 and repayment of fuel financing in the first half (Q2 page:8). - Quarterly operating income moved from a loss of 41 in Q1 2026 to 446 in Q2 and 115 in Q3, so the first nine months total 521 against 1,015 a year earlier. - Net debt on the management definition fell to 28,079 from 27,438... see note: the management total debt rose from 34,732 at March 31, 2026 to 36,366 at September 30, 2026 (D1 page:11, D3 page:10), reversing the Q1 low that D1 page:6 calls the first time under 35 billion since mid-2015. The 2023 to 3Q26 net debt chart labels in D3 page:6 show a lower figure than the year before, but the Q1 to Q3 2026 sequence in the reconciliations shows net debt higher at September 30 than at March 31.

facts.label: Credit read-through
facts.text: - Earnings carry little cushion against debt service. LTM EBITDA of 2,891 on the income statement lines covers interest expense, net only 1.74 times, and operating income does not cover it. Fuel price, not volume, drove the Q3 decline; the fourth-quarter outlook assumes a higher fuel price than the third quarter (D3 page:6), and the full-year adjusted loss per share outlook was widened lower from the July outlook (D2 page:6; D3 page:6). - Leverage on any basis in the sources is well above management's 3.0 times target: management's own net debt of 28,079 is 6.80 times the LTM EBITDAR built from income statement lines (CALC C13). Management's adjusted EBITDAR includes regional depreciation and rent and is not supplied for any period after Q1 2026, so this ratio is conservative in the sense of being lower on EBITDAR and should be read as indicative; the gap to the target is large under any plausible definition. - Liquidity is the offset: 11.8 billion of liquidity, no revolver draws and more than 26 billion of unencumbered assets and first-lien borrowing capacity per management (D3 page:6). The management claim on unencumbered assets is unverified in the filings supplied. - Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2028. The 2028 principal of 7,861 for American is the peak, and the secured nature of nearly all debt means asset-backed refinancing capacity (EETCs, equipment loans) is the main route, as 2026 activity shows. - Structural points for the issuer: American holds 10,430 of related-party receivables from affiliates, which makes up a large part of its current assets (Q3 page:26), and the PSP notes of 3,746 sit at AAG, not American. American's own total debt and finance leases are 25,876 against 29,635 at AAG.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: yield-driven revenue growth with lower load factor (Q3 page:44, page:47) and large loyalty and air traffic liabilities (Q3 page:13). Mechanic: price-led revenue is exposed to demand elasticity and fare pressure, while customer prepayments and partner cash dampen near-term volatility. Implication: revenue is large and recurring but not contractual; liquidity depends on float that can unwind. Counter-evidence: record revenue in each of the last three quarters per the decks; no conflict logged. - Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: fuel up and no hedges (Q3 page:44), non-fuel costs rising faster than capacity (Q3 page:47). Mechanic: unhedged fuel and sticky labor cost compress operating margin to near break-even, so interest and debt service must be met from float, asset financing and liquidity. Implication: coverage is thin and the credit relies on external secured financing access; this is a key uncertainty. - Concentration. Evidence: reliance on Citi, Mastercard, joint business partners and a few hubs (K25 page:11 to page:13). Mechanic: a change in a partner contract changes cash inflow or network reach. Implication: monitor partner agreements; no covenant detail is supplied. - Collateral and structure. Evidence: secured debt dominates and unsecured PSP notes sit at AAG (CP-1 rows). Mechanic: American's lenders hold liens on aircraft and loyalty assets while parent-level creditors have structurally junior claims on American's equity. Implication: recovery prospects differ by instrument and depend on collateral value, which is Not supplied. - Sponsor alignment: not applicable, no sponsor.

Mechanic: American's lenders hold liens on aircraft and loyalty assets while parent-level creditors have structurally junior claims on American's equity. Implication: recovery prospects differ by instrument and depend on collateral value, which is Not supplied.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: American Airlines, Inc. is a large, liquid but heavily indebted network carrier whose current earnings are too thin to service its debt without continued access to secured financing. The strongest support is USD 11,763 million of available liquidity at September 30, 2026, with nothing drawn on revolving facilities and almost all debt backed by identified collateral. The weakest point is unhedged fuel: a 62.7% higher fuel price per gallon cut third-quarter operating income to USD 115 million on USD 16,335 million of revenue, and last-twelve-month EBITDA covered net interest only 1.74x. The outcome turns on fuel prices, whether yield-led revenue holds, and the USD 7,861 million of principal due in 2028. Confidence is Medium (Analyst Interpretation). [CP-1 table; CP-1A operating model]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, earnings are the pressure point, not liquidity. Revenue grew 19.3% in the third quarter of 2026 to USD 16,335 million, but fuel expense rose USD 1,868 million to USD 4,635 million and operating income fell to USD 115 million from USD 151 million; the pre-tax loss widened to USD 334 million from USD 142 million (Documentary Fact; CP-1 table). Nine-month operating income was USD 521 million against USD 1,015 million a year earlier. The mechanism is that the company carries no fuel hedges and recaptures higher fuel only through fares, so a fuel move reaches operating income and cash flow within the same quarter (Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Liquidity: USD 11,763 million at American and USD 11,797 million at AAG, up from USD 9,233 million at December 31, 2025 at AAG, with no revolver draw, gives the issuer time to absorb a fuel shock (Documentary Fact). Financing access: the issuer raised about USD 4,100 million of aircraft-backed debt in the first nine months of 2026, repaid USD 1,000 million of 8.50% secured notes and a USD 629 million term loan, and extended its largest bank maturities, which shows market access and lowers near-term refinancing risk (Documentary Fact). Franchise and cash generation from loyalty partners, with USD 6,200 million of partner cash in 2025, supports revenue visibility and collateral value (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the premium and corporate growth claims). Capital allocation: no dividends or share repurchases in 2025 or 2024, and prepayments of expensive secured debt in 2026, are creditor-supportive actions (Documentary Fact). Scale and network: nine hubs, over 350 destinations and a mainline fleet in which 547 of 1,013 aircraft are owned give a large collateral base for asset-backed financing (Documentary Fact).

Earnings and coverage: operating income is near break-even in the latest quarter and below net interest on a last-twelve-month basis (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the coverage ratios). Unhedged fuel exposure: the company states it does not hedge and fuel price per gallon rose 62.7% in the third quarter, with management guiding to a full-year adjusted loss per share (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the guidance). Leverage: management net debt of USD 28,079 million against a stated 3.0x target is a long way from target, and the company is still adding secured aircraft debt to fund USD 24,056 million of aircraft and engine purchase commitments (Documentary Fact). Cost inflation outside fuel: management's CASM excluding special items, fuel and profit sharing rose 3.0% while load factor fell 2.6 points, and mainline pilot, mechanic and fleet service contracts become amendable in 2027, inside the debt maturity window (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the CASM measure). Structural subordination: the unsecured PSP notes sit at the parent and American's own creditors rank against encumbered assets whose value is not disclosed (Analyst Interpretation). Transparency: covenant thresholds, executed documents and affiliate balance terms are not in the supplied sources, so covenant headroom cannot be tested (Insufficient Information).

## Findings
### Overall source-sufficiency read

The effective source set is one audited annual report, three unaudited quarterly reports and three management earnings decks, all from the issuer and all dated on or before 2026-10-22, inside the 2026-11-05 cutoff. The two filing families control their own facts; the decks are attributed management claims and cannot override a filing. For a credit snapshot of American Airlines, Inc. the set is sufficient to proceed, with bounded limitations. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY: nothing here evaluates downstream model input contracts, normalizes quarters or reconciles figures (CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED).

Evidence to source risk to consequence: the filings are combined AAG and American filings (C4, C11), so AAG-level and American-level statements both sit in each file; the risk is that a figure is read from the wrong perimeter, which would mislead CP-1 if left unmarked. The strongest contrary evidence to a clean READY is that no executed financing document, indenture or credit agreement is supplied (the run context says none, and the exhibit lists only incorporate such documents by reference, C9, C28), so covenant terms are known only through the filings' summaries (C23 to C26). Consequence: debt, maturity and liquidity work can proceed from the filings, but legal-term detail is limited to what the filings state, and the next evidence action is to obtain the executed credit agreements and indentures if covenant levels or baskets are needed.
### Entity and perimeter

- American Airlines, Inc. (American) is the requested issuer. It is the wholly-owned subsidiary of American Airlines Group Inc. (AAG), which holds all 1,000 shares of American (C2, C4), and it files its own statements in Item 8B of the 10-K and Item 1B of each 10-Q (C11). It has its own commission file number (C1, C10).
- American meets the conditions for the reduced disclosure format (C3), so Part III information is omitted for American; this is not an evidence gap for credit work.

- AAG is the listed parent (ticker AAL per the run context). Parent-level debt is visible: the unsecured PSP1 note is listed in the debt table (C18) and the 10-K contractual-obligations table shows a separate block for "AAG Parent and Other AAG Subsidiaries" (C6) alongside the American block (C5).

- The two perimeters carry different figures for the same line items, for example total available liquidity of AAG and of American (C22) and AAG's balance sheet against American's, which includes related-party receivables (C20). The decks speak only for AAG. No guarantor list is supplied: the run context lists no guarantors, and which entity borrows or guarantees each facility is stated only in prose in the debt note (for example that American and AAG entered into the credit agreement amendments, page:16 of the third-quarter 10-Q). The guarantor and restricted-group perimeter of each instrument is therefore an unresolved distinction (see Gaps).
### Document family, authority and version relationships

- The 10-K (audited, FY2025) is the base annual source. The three 10-Qs (March 31, June 30 and September 30, 2026; C32, C31, C10) are separate active sources, not replacements: each covers its own period and the later ones carry year-to-date columns that overlap the earlier ones. No document supersedes another, and none is treated as a duplicate.
- The third-quarter 10-Q is the latest filing and was signed October 22, 2026 (C27), the same date as the third-quarter deck.

- The three decks are separate quarterly presentations, each attributed to management; none repeats another. Their figures (for example C33, C40) are management non-GAAP measures and must be tied to the filings before use.
- Duplicates: none identified. The same financial statements appear once for AAG and once for American inside each filing; these are distinct perimeters, not duplicates.
- No draft or unsigned material is supplied. The 10-K signature page is dated February 18, 2026 and the third-quarter 10-Q October 22, 2026 (C27).

- Nothing supplied post-dates the 2026-11-05 cutoff. Events after September 30, 2026 appear only as forward statements in the third-quarter deck (for example the fuel-curve date of October 19 and fourth-quarter outlook, C36) and are management outlook, not reported results.
### Coverage by profile

- Financial reports (10-K and 10-Qs). Located content covers statements of operations, balance sheets, cash flows, debt notes, liquidity, covenant text, and operating statistics (C30) in the third-quarter 10-Q; the 10-K additionally has the single-segment disclosure (C29), multi-year selected data (C7), a contractual-obligations maturity table (C5, C6) and cash interest paid (C8); the 10-Qs were not found to repeat a segment note. The converted text is complete in page order from cover to signatures for all four filings (10-K page:1 to page:314; 10-Qs page:1 to the signature pages; third-quarter 10-Q page:1 to page:73 ending with the signatures, C27). Extraction status is not a fidelity review: numbers have not been checked against the original HTML.

- Debt and liquidity. The third-quarter 10-Q lists each secured and unsecured facility by name, rate, maturity and balance (C16, C18), the undrawn facilities (C17) and the liquidity table (C21, C22). Covenant disclosure is descriptive: LTV or collateral coverage ratio covenants, a minimum liquidity covenant of $2.0 billion, and a peak debt service coverage ratio for the AAdvantage Financing (C23 to C25), with a statement of compliance (C26). Numeric LTV and coverage thresholds are not stated in the text located.

- Earnings releases. No earnings release is supplied as a separate document. The three decks are the only management quarter-by-quarter claims and they carry GAAP to non-GAAP reconciliations (for example C37), guidance and attributed narrative. The 10-Qs give discrete three-month and nine-month income statement columns (C12), but the cash flow statement is year-to-date only (C13), so discrete third-quarter cash flow is not stated in one source (see Gaps).

- Decks. Only the text layer was extracted. Charts, images and speaker notes are not covered. In the third-quarter deck the net debt chart shows its values as loose text without axis mapping (C35), which cannot be tied to a series from text alone, although the appendix table states the figure in words and numbers (C33).

- Legal and financing sources. None supplied. The 10-K and the third-quarter 10-Q exhibit lists name credit agreements and amendments that are incorporated by reference (C9, C28) but their text is not in the pack. These are named, not retained.
- Workbooks and scans: none supplied.

| CP-1 (financial data and debt) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs discrete periods, debt by facility, maturities, liquidity, cash interest. Located in C12, C13, C14, C16 to C18, C21, C22, C5, C8. | Cash flow is YTD only in each 10-Q; cash taxes paid not located; AAG and American perimeters both present; finance lease detail sits outside the debt table (C15 shows a balance sheet line that includes finance leases); no executed debt documents. |

| CP-1A (business and transaction context) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs ownership, business model, history. Located in C4, C2, C29, 10-K Item 1 (page:9 onward) and deck narrative slides. | No transaction documents; ownership of the equity beyond the parent-subsidiary link is not needed for the subsidiary but is not supplied for AAG holders; deck charts and images not inspected. |

| CP-2 (credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Depends on CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, which the dependency planner sequences; source sufficiency is not conditional on them. | Inherits the CP-1 and CP-1A limitations; no ratings, quotes or valuation inputs in the run context. |

| CP-5 (evidence trace validator) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs retained quotes that can be matched to the pack; the pinned text supports that. | Quote matching confirms text presence, not original-document fidelity; deck chart content cannot be traced. |
None of the consumers is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. No source with blocked preparation exists, so none was excluded or used as a fallback.
### Conflicts

No conflict between sources was found at the level CP-0 reads. One difference needs explanation downstream rather than being a conflict: the third-quarter deck states debt and finance leases of $29,635 million (C33) while the debt note total is $29,321 million (C16) and the balance sheet shows current maturities of $3,692 million (C15); the deck and balance sheet lines include finance leases and the note table is stated before unamortized discount, premium and issuance costs. This is a presentation basis difference to be resolved by CP-1 with locators, not a document conflict, and CP-0 does not reconcile it.
## Calculations

No figure was calculated, normalized or reconciled in this module, as the method requires. The only counts used are coverage counts: the 10-K converted text runs from page:1 to page:314, the third-quarter 10-Q from page:1 to page:73, and the three decks have 11 (first quarter), 9 (second quarter) and 10 (third quarter) text pages; the decks print slide numbers up to 18, 14 and 16, respectively, so text pages do not equal slides. Page counts do not establish readiness. Differences between debt measures noted under Conflicts are stated without arithmetic and are left to CP-1.
## Gaps
| Id | Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| G1 | No executed credit agreements, indentures, EETC documents or amendments are supplied; covenant levels, baskets, guarantor lists and collateral definitions are known only from filing summaries (C23 to C26, C9). The run context lists no guarantors. | Medium | CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 | Obtain the executed documents named in the exhibit lists if covenant or guarantor detail is required. Until then state covenants as filing-summary level only. |

| G2 | Guarantor and restricted-group perimeter per instrument is unresolved; some facilities are at AAG parent level (C6, C18), others at American, and the AAdvantage Financing is borrowed by American and AAdvantage Loyalty IP Ltd. (C9). | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Resolve by instrument from the debt note and exhibits; keep AAG and American figures labelled. |

| G3 | Cash flow statements are year-to-date in each 10-Q (C13), so a discrete third-quarter cash flow is not stated in a single source. | Low | CP-1 | Derive downstream from the nine-month and six-month filings with both locators; CP-0 does not derive it. |

| G4 | Cash taxes paid was not located in the supplemental cash flow lines of the 10-K or third-quarter 10-Q (interest paid is, C8, C14). Not supplied there; not zero. | Low | CP-1 | Search the income tax notes; otherwise mark Not supplied. |

| G5 | Numeric LTV, collateral coverage and peak debt service coverage thresholds are not stated in the located covenant text (C23 to C25). Compliance is asserted (C26) without ratios. | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Not supplied; obtain executed documents (G1) or mark Not supplied. |

| G6 | Decks: charts, images and speaker notes were not inspected; the text pages do not map to slides (11, 9 and 10 text pages against printed slide numbers up to 18, 14 and 16). Chart series such as C35 cannot be read from text alone. | Low | CP-1A, CP-5 | Use deck text only as attributed claims; do not claim slide-level coverage. |

| G7 | The second-quarter deck contains no debt, net debt, liquidity or free cash flow reconciliation page in the located text; the first-quarter deck has them (C39, C40) and the third-quarter deck has the net debt table (C33) but no free cash flow table. Management measures are therefore not available for every quarter. | Low | CP-1 | Use filings for every quarter; treat deck measures as supporting. |

| G8 | Balance sheet debt lines include finance leases while the Note 5 table does not (C15, C16); finance lease balances are in the lease notes and were not located here at facility level. Facility-level carrying values must be tied to the balance sheet downstream. | Medium | CP-1 | Locate the lease note and tie by period; keep unamortized costs separate. |
| G9 | No credit ratings, market quotes, valuation inputs, peer data or deal terms are supplied (run context blanks). Absent, not zero. | Low | CP-2 | Not supplied; do not infer. |

| G10 | Extraction fidelity of the converted text against the original filings has not been reviewed; the inner header hashes of the files differ from the pinned hashes. | Low | All | Treat quotes as extraction-level evidence; spot-check against the originals if a figure is decisive. |

| G11 | The 10-K figures are FY2025 and pre-date the 2026 refinancings; the third-quarter 10-Q shows 2026 amendments and new facilities (page:16 and page:17). Year-end debt terms should not be carried into the current period. | Low | CP-1 | Use the third-quarter 10-Q for the current structure and the 10-K only for the prior period (fy-2025). |
## Next module

Proceed to CP-1 (financial data and debt) with the full pinned source set, then CP-1A, then CP-2 and CP-5 as sequenced by the dependency planner. Carry gaps G1 to G11 forward as limitations. The next evidence action is to obtain the executed credit agreements and indentures (G1, G5) if covenant levels or guarantor perimeter are decision drivers; otherwise proceed on filing summaries and label them as such.

### Debt structure

- Instruments are mostly secured. Secured debt is 25,575 of 29,321 in Note 5 and is made up of term loans under the 2013, 2014 and 2023 credit facilities, 7.25% and 5.75% senior secured notes, the AAdvantage Financing, EETCs, equipment loans and special facility revenue bonds (Q3 page:14 and page:15). Secured financings are collateralized by aircraft, engines, simulators, airport gate leasehold rights, route authorities, airport slots, certain receivables, certain intellectual property and certain loyalty program assets (Q3 page:16).

- The only unsecured debt in Note 5 is the three PSP promissory notes, 3,746 in total. In the contractual obligations table they sit under AAG Parent and Other AAG Subsidiaries and fall due in 2030 and 2031 (Q3 page:66), so they are a parent-level claim that is outside the American maturity table. American's own table totals 25,575 of principal, equal to the secured subtotal.

- Two loan families are tied to the AAdvantage loyalty program: the AAdvantage Financing is borrowed by American and AAdvantage Loyalty IP Ltd. and carries a peak debt service coverage ratio (Q3 page:17 and page:61).

- Rates: the named term loans and PSP notes are floating (5.94% to 6.76% at September 30, 2026) and total 10,869, 37% of Note 5 debt before counting variable-rate equipment loans, which are inside the 4,926 line.

- Bonds versus loans: the senior secured notes outstanding are the 7.25% notes (750) and the 5.75% notes (2,750); the 8.50% notes (1,000) were prepaid in full and the 5.50% notes (583 at year end) are nil at September 30, 2026. Most of the remaining debt is bank term loans, EETC pass-through certificates (9,332, up from 6,912) and equipment loans, not capital markets bonds.

- 2026 financing activity (Q3 page:16 to page:20, page:45 and page:46): revolving commitments of the 2013, 2014 and 2023 facilities were reset to mature in March 2031; the 2014 term loans due January 2027 were refinanced to May 2033 with 703 of incremental term loans; the 2025 AAdvantage term loan margin was reduced; 8.50% secured notes of 1.0 billion and the 629 senior short-term term loan were repaid; 310 of EETC equipment notes were prepaid; and about 4.1 billion of EETC, equipment loan and other note proceeds were raised, including 2026-1, 2026-2 and engine EETCs. Of the 2026-2 EETC proceeds, about 633 remain in escrow and are not reported as American debt (Q3 page:19).

- Maturity profile (American principal): 631 in the remainder of 2026, 3,550 in 2027, 7,861 in 2028, 3,884 in 2029, 972 in 2030 and 8,677 from 2031 (Q3 page:65). The 2028 column is the largest single year and is more than twice the 2027 figure. The sources do not break the 2028 amount down by instrument; named instruments due in 2028 in Note 5 are the 2013 term loan (960, February), the 7.25% notes (750, February) and the 2021 AAdvantage term loan (2,247, April), which do not explain the whole column because installment and equipment debt also amortizes into 2028. Remainder of 2026 through 2028 principal totals 12,042 against available liquidity of 11,797.
### Liquidity and covenants

- Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was 11,797 for AAG and 11,763 for American, comprising cash 1,124, short-term investments 7,163 and undrawn facilities 3,510 (Q3 page:59 and page:60). It was 9,233 at December 31, 2025. Restricted cash and short-term investments of 555 are excluded.

- Nothing is drawn on the revolving and other facilities (Q3 page:16). One 350 revolver was extended to March 2028 and a 50 cargo receivables facility expires in December 2026 (Q3 page:16), so undrawn capacity of 3,510 is not all long-dated.

- Covenants are described, not quantified: loan to value or collateral coverage ratio covenants with cure through additional collateral, cash held in accounts, paydown or a higher interest rate; a minimum of 2.0 billion of unrestricted cash plus availability under revolving facilities in a significant portion of agreements; and a peak debt service coverage ratio in the AAdvantage Financing that can trigger early repayment. Management states compliance at the latest measurement dates (Q3 page:61). Thresholds, test dates and headroom are not in the supplied text.

- The liquidity covenant row above uses cash plus undrawn facilities only and omits short-term investments, because the covenant text does not say whether they count; it shows ample indicative headroom but is not a covenant calculation.

- The reported improvement in liquidity since year end coincides with a larger air traffic liability and loyalty program liability, which the 10-Q names as the main driver of nine-month operating cash flow (Q3 page:61). That inflow is seasonal and customer-funded; it is not earnings-driven.
### Latest quarter changes (Q3 2026 against Q3 2025)

- Revenue rose 19.3% to 16,335 on yield and loyalty, with load factor down 2.6 points and capacity up 4.2% (Q3 page:43, page:44 and page:47). Fuel expense rose by 1,868 to 4,635 on a 62.7% higher price per gallon, absorbing the revenue gain; operating income fell to 115 from 151 and the pre-tax loss widened to 334 from 142. No fuel hedges were outstanding (Q3 page:44).

- Non-fuel cost pressure: management's CASM excluding special items, fuel and profit sharing rose 3.0% to 14.34 cents; salaries, wages and benefits rose 252 and other operating expenses rose 237 (Q3 page:47 and page:50).

- Net loss of 269 included pre-tax net special items of 112, mainly an impairment of the equity investment in Republic Airways Holdings and mark-to-market losses on equity investments (Q3 page:51). Interest expense, net was essentially flat at 435.

- Derived discrete Q3 operating cash flow was negative and discrete Q3 capex was the largest of the year (CALC C7), after strong first-half inflows, which includes the first-quarter operating cash flow of 4,223 and repayment of fuel financing in the first half (Q2 page:8).
- Quarterly operating income moved from a loss of 41 in Q1 2026 to 446 in Q2 and 115 in Q3, so the first nine months total 521 against 1,015 a year earlier.

- Net debt on the management definition fell to 28,079 from 27,438... see note: the management total debt rose from 34,732 at March 31, 2026 to 36,366 at September 30, 2026 (D1 page:11, D3 page:10), reversing the Q1 low that D1 page:6 calls the first time under 35 billion since mid-2015. The 2023 to 3Q26 net debt chart labels in D3 page:6 show a lower figure than the year before, but the Q1 to Q3 2026 sequence in the reconciliations shows net debt higher at September 30 than at March 31.
### Credit read-through

- Earnings carry little cushion against debt service. LTM EBITDA of 2,891 on the income statement lines covers interest expense, net only 1.74 times, and operating income does not cover it. Fuel price, not volume, drove the Q3 decline; the fourth-quarter outlook assumes a higher fuel price than the third quarter (D3 page:6), and the full-year adjusted loss per share outlook was widened lower from the July outlook (D2 page:6; D3 page:6).

- Leverage on any basis in the sources is well above management's 3.0 times target: management's own net debt of 28,079 is 6.80 times the LTM EBITDAR built from income statement lines (CALC C13). Management's adjusted EBITDAR includes regional depreciation and rent and is not supplied for any period after Q1 2026, so this ratio is conservative in the sense of being lower on EBITDAR and should be read as indicative; the gap to the target is large under any plausible definition.

- Liquidity is the offset: 11.8 billion of liquidity, no revolver draws and more than 26 billion of unencumbered assets and first-lien borrowing capacity per management (D3 page:6). The management claim on unencumbered assets is unverified in the filings supplied.

- Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2028. The 2028 principal of 7,861 for American is the peak, and the secured nature of nearly all debt means asset-backed refinancing capacity (EETCs, equipment loans) is the main route, as 2026 activity shows.

- Structural points for the issuer: American holds 10,430 of related-party receivables from affiliates, which makes up a large part of its current assets (Q3 page:26), and the PSP notes of 3,746 sit at AAG, not American. American's own total debt and finance leases are 25,876 against 29,635 at AAG.
### Subsequent events and forward statements

- After September 30, 2026 the 10-Q records the exercise of purchase options for five Airbus A320 Family aircraft in October 2026 and a commitment to buy two Boeing 777-200ER aircraft off-lease in the fourth quarter of 2026 (Q3 page:65). An October 2026 court filing in the Northeast Alliance antitrust matter is also noted (Q3 page:42). No debt issuance or repayment after September 30 is reported in the sources.
- The fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 outlook figures are management forecasts as of October 22, 2026 and are not reported results.

Check totals: American principal 631 + 3,550 + 7,861 + 3,884 + 972 + 8,677 = 25,575; plus AAG parent 3,746 = 29,321, equal to the Note 5 total.
## Gaps

- Executed credit agreements, indentures and EETC documents are not supplied (CP-0 G1): covenant thresholds, test dates, cure mechanics, guarantors and collateral definitions are known only from filing summaries. Covenant compliance headroom is Not calculable.

- Management adjusted EBITDAR is supplied only for Q1 2026 (D1 page:11). LTM EBITDA and EBITDAR here use income statement lines, which exclude regional depreciation and rent that sit in regional expenses and the cash flow D&A of 2,219 for FY2025 (K25 page:143); management leverage cannot be reproduced and the 3.0 times target is not comparable. Regional operating special items of 8 are not added to the special items line.

- Nine-month cash flow statements in the 10-Qs are condensed: operating cash flow components, working capital lines and income taxes paid are not shown, so cash taxes are Not supplied (the tax benefit is described as substantially non-cash, Q3 page:20) and cash flow quality cannot be split beyond the narrative drivers.
- Discrete Q3 cash flow is derived by difference across two filings, not printed (C7).

- Finance lease liabilities are only available as undiscounted obligations of 834 for American and 17 for AAG parent (Q3 page:65, page:66); the carrying amount inside the 29,635 is not separately supplied, and the Note 5 total of 29,321 less discount of 346 does not equal the balance sheet debt line because the balance sheet line includes finance leases. No reconciliation between them is supplied.
- Instrument-level detail of the 2028 maturity of 7,861 and the call or amortization terms of EETCs and equipment loans are not supplied.

- Management claims of more than 26 billion of unencumbered assets and first-lien borrowing capacity (D3 page:6) and the net debt chart series (D3 page:6) cannot be tied to filings or to chart axes from text.

- Pension obligations of 92 in the management total debt (D3 page:10) differ from the pension and postretirement liability of 1,099 on the balance sheet (Q3 page:7); the measure is management defined and the difference is not explained in the sources.
- Guarantor and restricted group perimeter by instrument is unresolved (CP-0 G2); AAG and American figures are labelled but intercompany funding terms behind the 10,430 receivable are Not supplied.
- No ratings, market prices or yields are supplied, so market-based leverage and relative value are Not calculable.
- Extraction fidelity has not been reviewed against the original HTML (CP-0 G10).
## Next module

Proceed to CP-1A (business and transaction context) with the CP-0 and CP-1 handoffs. Carry forward: the fuel-price sensitivity (no hedges), the loyalty program as collateral for the AAdvantage Financing, the parent and issuer perimeter split of the PSP notes and affiliate receivables, the 2028 maturity concentration, and the covenant detail that only the executed documents can supply.

Repayments in 2026 include the 629 senior short-term term loan and the 8.50% senior secured notes of 1.0 billion, plus 310 of EETC equipment notes prepaid.

The October 2026 option exercise for five Airbus A320 Family aircraft and the commitment to buy two Boeing 777-200ER aircraft off-lease in the fourth quarter of 2026 (Q3 page:65) are subsequent events to the September 30 balance sheet and are not included in the period facts above.

- 2013: merger with US Airways Group, Inc. (K25 page:150, goodwill note). Terms, financing and integration costs are Not supplied in the pack.

- 2025: 40 mainline aircraft delivered; 2025 AAdvantage term loan and 2025-1 aircraft EETCs issued; PSP promissory notes outstanding (K25 page:100; Q3 page:14, page:18). The PSP issue dates and origin are Not supplied beyond their names.
- 2026: refinancings listed above; Republic Holdings impairment in Q3 (Q3 page:22).
- After September 30, 2026: aircraft purchase option exercise and off-lease commitment (Subsequent event); fourth quarter and full year outlook issued October 22, 2026 (D3 page:6).

- Documented actions only, issuer level. Supportive indicators: no dividends and no share repurchases in 2025 or 2024; 2026 repayment or prepayment of the senior short-term term loan, the 8.50% secured notes and part of the EETC equipment notes; management states a net debt to EBITDAR target of 3.0 times (D3 page:6; Management Language). Neutral or mixed: the same management says it is committed to a leverage target that the CP-1 calculation shows is far from met on the available data, and the company keeps adding secured aircraft debt for fleet growth. No documented creditor-adverse action (priming, uptiering, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release) appears in the supplied sources. Intercompany behaviour: American carries a large receivable from related parties (CP-1 row), whose terms are Not supplied.

- Legal capacity versus willingness versus feasibility: capacity (what debt documents permit) is limited to the summary that agreements contain customary negative covenants restricting additional indebtedness, dividends and repurchases (Q3 page:61); willingness is shown by the actions above; feasibility rests on liquidity and market access shown by 2026 issuance. Evidence quality: High for filings, Low for management deck claims.
- Scoring dimensions are not scored here; they are left to the Python assembler.
### Credit translations

- Revenue durability. Evidence: yield-driven revenue growth with lower load factor (Q3 page:44, page:47) and large loyalty and air traffic liabilities (Q3 page:13). Mechanic: price-led revenue is exposed to demand elasticity and fare pressure, while customer prepayments and partner cash dampen near-term volatility. Implication: revenue is large and recurring but not contractual; liquidity depends on float that can unwind. Counter-evidence: record revenue in each of the last three quarters per the decks; no conflict logged.

- Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: fuel up and no hedges (Q3 page:44), non-fuel costs rising faster than capacity (Q3 page:47). Mechanic: unhedged fuel and sticky labor cost compress operating margin to near break-even, so interest and debt service must be met from float, asset financing and liquidity. Implication: coverage is thin and the credit relies on external secured financing access; this is a key uncertainty.

- Concentration. Evidence: reliance on Citi, Mastercard, joint business partners and a few hubs (K25 page:11 to page:13). Mechanic: a change in a partner contract changes cash inflow or network reach. Implication: monitor partner agreements; no covenant detail is supplied.

- Collateral and structure. Evidence: secured debt dominates and unsecured PSP notes sit at AAG (CP-1 rows). Mechanic: American's lenders hold liens on aircraft and loyalty assets while parent-level creditors have structurally junior claims on American's equity. Implication: recovery prospects differ by instrument and depend on collateral value, which is Not supplied.

One presentation difference is logged for the committee: management's total debt measure and the Note 5 debt table are on different bases (CP-1 gaps) and the PSP notes appear in the AAG parent column of the maturity table but are described by the company as part of AAG's debt. Both are quoted in the CP-1 handoff; this module does not reconcile them.

The correct reading of its own sources is: management net debt was 27,438 at March 31, 2026 (D1 page:11) and 28,079 at September 30, 2026 (D3 page:10), so net debt rose, and total debt rose from 34,732 to 36,366 over the same dates. ## Findings
### Credit view

American Airlines, Inc. is a large, liquid but heavily indebted network carrier whose current earnings are too thin to service its debt without continued access to secured financing. The strongest support is USD 11,763 million of available liquidity at September 30, 2026, with nothing drawn on revolving facilities and almost all debt backed by identified collateral. The weakest point is unhedged fuel: a 62.7% higher fuel price per gallon cut third-quarter operating income to USD 115 million on USD 16,335 million of revenue, and last-twelve-month EBITDA covered net interest only 1.74x. The outcome turns on fuel prices, whether yield-led revenue holds, and the USD 7,861 million of principal due in 2028. Confidence is Medium (Analyst Interpretation). [CP-1 table; CP-1A operating model]
### Key findings

First, earnings are the pressure point, not liquidity. Revenue grew 19.3% in the third quarter of 2026 to USD 16,335 million, but fuel expense rose USD 1,868 million to USD 4,635 million and operating income fell to USD 115 million from USD 151 million; the pre-tax loss widened to USD 334 million from USD 142 million (Documentary Fact; CP-1 table). Nine-month operating income was USD 521 million against USD 1,015 million a year earlier. The mechanism is that the company carries no fuel hedges and recaptures higher fuel only through fares, so a fuel move reaches operating income and cash flow within the same quarter (Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model).

Second, leverage is high on every measure the sources allow. Management's own net debt was USD 28,079 million at September 30, 2026, up from USD 27,438 million at March 31, 2026; against last-twelve-month EBITDAR built from income statement lines of USD 4,127 million that is 6.80x, versus management's stated target of 3.0x (Documentary Fact for the debt figures, Analyst Interpretation for the ratio; CP-1 calculation C13). The ratio omits regional depreciation and rent, so management's own adjusted measure would differ, but the gap to the target is large on any definition the sources support. This also corrects a garbled bullet in the CP-1 handoff, which should have said that net debt rose between those dates.

Third, debt service rests on liquidity and refinancing access more than on earnings. Last-twelve-month operating income of USD 973 million was below net interest expense of USD 1,664 million, and last-twelve-month free cash flow on a simple definition was negative USD 91 million (Documentary Fact; CP-1 calculations C6 and C8). Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 4,541 million was helped by a rise in air traffic and loyalty liabilities, and the derived third-quarter operating cash flow was negative USD 153 million with third-quarter capex of USD 1,095 million (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 calculation C7). Customer-funded float lifts liquidity in good quarters and unwinds when bookings or mileage sales slow.

Fourth, the maturity profile is manageable near term and concentrated in 2028. American's principal due is USD 631 million for the remainder of 2026, USD 3,550 million in 2027 and USD 7,861 million in 2028, the peak year, against USD 11,797 million of AAG liquidity (Documentary Fact; CP-1 table). Nearly 87% of Note 5 debt is secured (CP-1 calculation C11), and 2026 refinancings pushed the 2014 term loans to May 2033 and revolvers to March 2031, so refinancing depends mainly on asset-backed markets for aircraft and loyalty collateral (Documentary Fact; CP-1A transaction summary). Nothing in the supplied sources shows how much headroom those collateral pools have.

Fifth, the business has real franchise support. Cash from co-branded credit card and other partners was USD 6,200 million in 2025, Citi became exclusive issuer of the co-branded portfolio in 2026, and premium and corporate revenue are growing per management (Documentary Fact for the partner cash, Management Language for the premium claims; CP-1A operating model). That cash is also the collateral base of the AAdvantage Financing, so it supports both revenue durability and secured borrowing capacity.

Sixth, structure matters for this issuer. The three PSP promissory notes of USD 3,746 million are the only unsecured debt and sit at the AAG parent, while American itself carries USD 25,876 million of debt and finance leases and a USD 10,430 million receivable from related parties (Documentary Fact; CP-1 table, CP-1A company profile). The terms of that affiliate receivable and the guarantor perimeter by instrument are not supplied, which limits any view of how value flows between American and its parent.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Liquidity: USD 11,763 million at American and USD 11,797 million at AAG, up from USD 9,233 million at December 31, 2025 at AAG, with no revolver draw, gives the issuer time to absorb a fuel shock (Documentary Fact). Financing access: the issuer raised about USD 4,100 million of aircraft-backed debt in the first nine months of 2026, repaid USD 1,000 million of 8.50% secured notes and a USD 629 million term loan, and extended its largest bank maturities, which shows market access and lowers near-term refinancing risk (Documentary Fact). Franchise and cash generation from loyalty partners, with USD 6,200 million of partner cash in 2025, supports revenue visibility and collateral value (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the premium and corporate growth claims). Capital allocation: no dividends or share repurchases in 2025 or 2024, and prepayments of expensive secured debt in 2026, are creditor-supportive actions (Documentary Fact). Scale and network: nine hubs, over 350 destinations and a mainline fleet in which 547 of 1,013 aircraft are owned give a large collateral base for asset-backed financing (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. Earnings and coverage: operating income is near break-even in the latest quarter and below net interest on a last-twelve-month basis (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the coverage ratios). Unhedged fuel exposure: the company states it does not hedge and fuel price per gallon rose 62.7% in the third quarter, with management guiding to a full-year adjusted loss per share (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the guidance). Leverage: management net debt of USD 28,079 million against a stated 3.0x target is a long way from target, and the company is still adding secured aircraft debt to fund USD 24,056 million of aircraft and engine purchase commitments (Documentary Fact). Cost inflation outside fuel: management's CASM excluding special items, fuel and profit sharing rose 3.0% while load factor fell 2.6 points, and mainline pilot, mechanic and fleet service contracts become amendable in 2027, inside the debt maturity window (Documentary Fact; Management Language for the CASM measure). Structural subordination: the unsecured PSP notes sit at the parent and American's own creditors rank against encumbered assets whose value is not disclosed (Analyst Interpretation). Transparency: covenant thresholds, executed documents and affiliate balance terms are not in the supplied sources, so covenant headroom cannot be tested (Insufficient Information).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Fuel price shock | Unhedged fuel and partial fare recapture compress operating income within a quarter | Thin coverage and weaker cash conversion; reliance on liquidity and secured financing | Critical |
| Leverage versus target | Net debt of USD 28,079 million is well above the 3.0x target on the available EBITDAR basis | Slow deleveraging path; sensitivity to any earnings miss | Material |
| 2028 maturity concentration | USD 7,861 million of American principal falls due in 2028 | Refinancing needs asset-backed market access in a peak year | Material |
| Float reversal | Rising air traffic and loyalty liabilities flattered nine-month cash flow | Liquidity could fall faster than earnings suggest if bookings or mileage sales weaken | Material |
| Capital commitments | USD 24,056 million of aircraft and engine purchase commitments | Continued secured borrowing and encumbrance of the fleet | Material |
| Labor cost reset | Major mainline contracts amendable in 2027 | Higher fixed cost or disruption while maturities are rising | Material |
| Covenants and collateral | Loan to value, minimum liquidity and debt service coverage tests exist but thresholds are not supplied | Cannot assess how close tests are in a downturn | Material |
| Parent and affiliate structure | Unsecured parent debt and a large affiliate receivable at American | Value leakage and ranking questions that documents would resolve | Minor |

None. CP-2 makes no new calculation and writes no figure that is not in the CP-1 handoff. Ratios cited (CP-1 calculations C6, C7, C8, C11 and C13) are the CP-1 results as written, with the CP-1 definition limits stated above.

- No recovery conclusion, relative value or instrument view is given; those belong to later modules. Severity: Minor.
